newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Nov 8.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Nov 8.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories on Friday:
- Eastman Kodak Co is having trouble establishing itself in South Africa again after having abandoned the market during apartheid.
- Retail stores reported better than expected same-store sales for October.
- Republic Industries Inc has signed an agreement to acquire Alamo Rent-a-Car Inc for $625 million in stock.
- A U.S. federal judge has frozen the assets of the chairman of a small company called Systems of Excellence Inc.
- U.S. liquor industry has ended its voluntary ban on liquor advertising on radio and television.
- The U.S. dollar fell against the Japanese yen following comments made by Japan's director general of the financial ministry's international finance bureau.
- U.S. treasury bond prices rose after an auction of a new 30-year bond.
- Borrowers in September paid off more credit card and other debt than usual.
- A one-time charge set back America Online Inc's revenues for the quarter.
- Manufactured Home Communities Inc made a new bid to buy Chateau Properties Inc.
- U.S. government has classified a set-top device made by Philips Electronics and Sony Corp as a weapon.
